extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings, and Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing imposition of reciprocal discipline by the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 (including notice/service, grounds to oppose, and post-discipline obligations). Applicable to respondents who have been disciplined by a state authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for reciprocal discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusion from practice before the USPTO may be imposed for violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), predicated upon being disbarred from the practice of law by a duly constituted authority of a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24; the USPTO may order exclusion in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters when predicated on state disbarment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and Order and opportunity to respond (40 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must send a 'Notice and Order Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' notifying the respondent that a Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline has been filed and providing an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to the state's discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order should inform the respondent of the grounds to oppose under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Service requirements when certified mail fails (37 C.F.R. § 11.35(a)(2)(i) and § 11.11(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: If certified mail delivery of the Notice and Order is not possible, service may be made via other means (here, UPS) at the most recent address provided to the OED Director pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.11(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document the method and receipt of service (e.g., UPS delivery) consistent with the cited regulations to establish proper service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible grounds to oppose reciprocal discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent may oppose imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to the state-imposed discipline based on one or more reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order must identify that these specific regulatory reasons exist and provide the respondent the chance to assert them within the 40-day period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to respond (no genuine issue of material fact)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent fails to file a response to the Notice and Order, the Office may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and impose reciprocal discipline accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-response can lead to entry of final order imposing exclusion identical to the state discipline without further factual dispute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imposition of identical reciprocal discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal discipline imposed by the USPTO may be identical to the discipline imposed by the state's highest authority (e.g., exclusion from practice before the USPTO effective the date of the Final Order).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order should specify the scope of exclusion (patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the USPTO) and its effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice in the Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette describing the exclusion, identifying the respondent, registration number, the fact of state disbarment, and the regulatory predicate (e.g., violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice should summarize the underlying state disciplinary findings and cite the authority for USPTO action (35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to disciplinary agencies, courts, and the public (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in states where the respondent is admitted, to courts where the respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the required notifications are made to the appropriate state agencies and courts as set out in § 11.59.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent duties following exclusion (37 C.F.R. § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent who is excluded shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those duties (as referenced) govern what excluded practitioners must do; the Final Order may expressly direct compliance with § 11.58.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI and prohibition on obtaining Customer Number
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will dissociate the respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure (PKI) certificate associated with those Customer Numbers; the respondent shall not apply for, obtain, or be added to a USPTO Customer Number unless and until reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an affirmative post-discipline constraint on electronic access and representation before the Office until reinstatement.
